title: Tiwary's Open Problem on Matching Lower Bound for Convex Independence in Minkowski Sums
statement_text: Does there exist a matching lower bound for $\mathrm{ci}(P + Q) = O\bigl((n+m)\log(n+m)\bigr)$ when $P$ and $Q$ are a convex $n$-gon and a convex $m$-gon, respectively?
context_text: Tiwary (2014) proved that $\mathrm{ci}(P+Q) = O((n+m)\log(n+m))$ when $P$ and $Q$ are convex polygons, remarking that the bound seemed very generous. He explicitly left as an open problem whether this upper bound is tight, i.e., whether a matching lower bound construction exists.
paper_contribution: Resolves the problem affirmatively by exhibiting families $(P_k)_{k>1}$ and $(Q_k)_{k>1}$ of convexly independent sets with $|P_k| = |Q_k| = 2^k$ and $\mathrm{ci}(P_k + Q_k) > (k+2)2^{k-1}$, establishing $\mathrm{ci}(P+Q) = \Theta(n \log n)$ for convex $n$-gons.
paper_title: Convexly independent subsets of Minkowski sums of convex polygons

title: Open Question on Convex Unit Distance Realization of Graphs $G_k$
statement_text: Can the graphs $G_k$ arising from the authors' construction of convex polygons $P_k,Q_k$ with $\mathrm{ci}(P_k+Q_k)\ge(k+2)2^{k-1}$ be realized as convex unit distance graphs?
context_text: A finite planar point set is convexly independent if it is the vertex set of a convex polygon, and $\mathrm{ci}(X)$ is the largest size of a convexly independent subset of $X$; $P+Q=\{p+q:p\in P,q\in Q\}$ is the Minkowski sum. Tiwary proved $\mathrm{ci}(P+Q)=O((n+m)\log(n+m))$ for a convex $n$-gon $P$ and a convex $m$-gon $Q$, and the authors show this is sharp: they construct convexly independent sets $P_k,Q_k$ of size $2^k$ with $\mathrm{ci}(P_k+Q_k)\ge(k+2)2^{k-1}$. The graph $G_k=(U_k\sqcup V_k,E_k)$ is the bipartite graph of this construction: its vertices are the $2^{k+1}$ points of $P_k$ and $Q_k$ (each side in convex position), and its $(k+2)2^{k-1}$ edges are the pairs $(p,q)\in P_k\times Q_k$ whose midpoints $(p+q)/2$ form the convexly independent set. A convex unit distance graph is the graph of unit-distance pairs among the vertices of a convex polygon; the Erdős–Moser problem asks for the maximum number of unit distances in a convex $n$-gon, for which the best upper bound is $O(n\log n)$ (Füredi, Aggarwal). The authors observe that if $G_k$ could be embedded with $U_k,V_k$ as south-east chains in the quadrant $\{x_1\ge0,x_2\le0\}$ and all edge midpoints on the unit circle, one would get convex $2^{k+1}$-gons with $\Theta(k2^k)$ unit diagonals, i.e. a matching $\Theta(n\log n)$ lower bound for the convex unit distance problem. Such an embedding cannot be excluded by the known list of forbidden matrices of Aggarwal, none of which appears in $G_k$; if $G_k$ is not realizable, it would be interesting to find a new forbidden pattern in $G_k$. The authors could neither construct such embeddings nor find such a pattern. This is a question of discrete geometry.
